q: The Gram-Schmidt process orthogonalises a linearly independent set {v₁,...,vₙ} to produce {u₁,...,uₙ}. In terms of matrix factorisations, this is equivalent to the:
opts: QR factorisation: A = QR with Q orthogonal and R upper triangular
exp: Gram-Schmidt gives the QR factorisation: if A = [v₁|…|vₙ], then A = QR where Q = [u₁|…|uₙ] (orthonormal columns) and R is upper triangular with positive diagonal (encoding the projection coefficients). QR factorisation is numerically more stable than normal equations for least squares.
